concepts.def: Macronutrient made of amino acids; provides 4 kcal/g; needed for growth and repair.
Nine amino acids the body cannot synthesise and must obtain from food.
Protein containing all essential amino acids — typically animal sources plus soya and quinoa.
Protein lacking one or more essential amino acids — most plant proteins.
Combining LBV foods (e.g. beans and rice) to provide all essential amino acids.
Unfolding of protein structure by heat, acid or agitation; e.g. egg white setting on cooking.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Priority Health Issues — a core area of A-Level Nutrition and Food Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Priority Health Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Priority Health Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
